block:acceleration_cavity: A copper RF cavity ringing at its resonant frequency. Its field points forward each time a bunch arrives, so particles gain energy on every pass.
block:basalt_column: Lava that cooled slowly and shrank as it set, cracking into columns, most often six-sided, as at the Giant's Causeway.
block:bubble_pedestal: The cradle on which a warp bubble is shaped. In Alcubierre's metric space contracts ahead and expands behind, while the bubble's own interior stays flat and calm.
block:cloud_seeder_stack: A stack that releases ice nuclei into supercooled cloud. Silver iodide, the usual agent, has a lattice so like ice that droplets freeze onto it and fall.
block:core_iron: The alloy of planetary cores and iron meteorites, roughly nine parts iron to one of nickel. Etched, it shows Widmanstätten patterns grown over millions of years.
block:decorative_telescope: A small reflecting telescope on its stand, still pointed at whatever its last observer wanted to see.
block:disk_confinement_ring: A ring of magnets that shapes the field around an accretion disk. In real disks, tangled fields drive the turbulence that lets gas shed its spin and fall inward.
block:entropy_sink: A copper heat sink for computation. By Landauer's principle every bit erased gives off at least kT ln 2 of heat, and something has to carry it away.
block:focus_receiver: The target at a lens's focal point, where light gathered over a broad aperture converges onto one small spot. It has to survive what it receives.
block:heliostat: A mirror that tracks the Sun on two axes. At Odeillo, sixty-three of them feed one parabolic concentrator whose focus passes 3,000 °C.
block:impact_chamber: An armoured chamber for hypervelocity tests. Above about 3 km/s, a projectile carries more energy per kilogram than the same mass of TNT.
block:lead_shielding_block: Dense lead for stopping gamma rays. Each half-value layer halves the dose; for the gammas of cobalt-60 that is about 1.2 cm of lead.
block:magnetite_block: Compacted Fe₃O₄, the most strongly magnetic mineral in nature. Lodestones, magnetite probably magnetised by lightning, made the first compasses.
block:microscope_column: The tube that holds a microscope's objective and eyepiece at a fixed distance apart. No light microscope resolves much finer than about 200 nm.
block:optical_bench: A rigid, flat rail on which lenses, slits and mirrors are clamped in line. Optics is mostly alignment, and this is where alignment is kept.
block:polished_dilithium: Dilithium cut and polished to a flawless face. Real dilithium, Li₂, is a fleeting molecule of lithium vapour; this crystal answers to fiction instead.
block:proof_membrane: A sheet stretched across the gap between premise and conclusion. Every step of the argument is a fibre in it, and one false step tears it through.
block:radium_lamp: Radium mixed with phosphor glows for years without power. The dial painters of the 1920s, who pointed their brushes with their lips, paid for that glow.
block:rf_oscillator: The heart of a cyclotron. It drives the gap at the cyclotron frequency, qB/2πm, which does not change with speed, so a circling particle is kicked every half turn.
block:seismic_isolator: Springs and dampers that cut a mirror off from the ground. Ground tremor dwarfs the 10⁻¹⁸ m a passing gravitational wave stretches an interferometer arm.
block:telescope_pier: A heavy masonry column for a telescope to stand on, built apart from the dome floor so that footsteps never shake the image.
block:tesla_toroid: The smooth metal doughnut atop a Tesla coil. Its broad curve spreads the charge and holds off corona, so the voltage climbs higher before sparks break out.
block:transition_valve: A valve that sends each state on to the next by fixed odds. It looks only at where things are, never at how they got there: the Markov property.
block:warp_coil_ring: One ring of a warp coil. The Alcubierre metric demands negative energy density, which no ordinary matter can supply in bulk.
item:pressure_suit_chestplate: A rigid shell built to bear the weight of rock overhead. At the base of Earth's mantle the pressure reaches about 136 GPa, over a million atmospheres.
item:refractory_suit_chestplate: Armour of refractory ceramics, which keep their strength where metals soften. Basaltic magma erupts at about 1,100 to 1,200 °C, and the suit hardly notices.
item:whipple_shield_chestplate: A thin bumper held off from the wall behind it. A micrometeoroid striking it shatters into a spreading cloud the inner layer can stop. Fred Whipple proposed it in the 1940s.
block:antiverse_cache: A locker for matter of the wrong sign. It holds its contents by fields alone, since a single touch of the walls would annihilate both.
entity:paradox_echo: A figure forever meeting its own past. It acts out the grandfather paradox, flickering whenever its history stops adding up.
block:pleroma_glass: Named for the Gnostics' Pleroma, the fullness of all that is. Light passes through it; nothing else is allowed to.
fluid:deep_brine: Ancient salt water from deep rock, many times saltier than the sea and often rich in lithium and boron. It has not seen daylight for millions of years.
block:lithostatic_casing: A casing built to bear the load of rock. In Earth's crust, lithostatic pressure rises by about 27 MPa for every kilometre of depth.
block:euclid_reliquary: A casket laid out in Euclid's proportions. The Elements rest on five postulates, and the fifth, on parallel lines, was doubted for two thousand years.
fluid:deuterium: Hydrogen with a neutron in its nucleus, about one atom in 6,400 in seawater. It fuses with tritium more readily than any other pair of nuclei.
fluid:radon: A noble gas born from the decay of radium. Radon-222 has a half-life of 3.8 days and is far heavier than air, so it pools in cellars and low places.
fluid:uranium_hexafluoride: The one uranium compound that is a gas near room temperature: it sublimes at 56.5 °C. Fluorine has a single isotope, so its molecules differ only by their uranium.
entity:black_swan: The rare, unforeseeable event, explained only afterwards. Europeans held every swan white until Dutch sailors met black ones in Australia in 1697; this one is seldom seen.
block:observatory_cache: A locker held in stasis by superconducting coils. Whoever sealed it meant the contents to be found exactly as they were left.
block:harmonic_pedestal: A pedestal tuned to resonance. What is set on it rings at whole-number multiples of one frequency, as the harmonics of a single string do.
block:unruh_ring_casing: Casing for a ring of extreme acceleration. An accelerated observer finds warm thermal radiation where an inertial one sees empty vacuum: the Unruh effect.
block:horizon_cache: A locker whose lid is an event horizon held open. While it stays shut, what is inside lies beyond the causal reach of everything else.
block:void_glass: Glass as dark as the space it came from. Gravity bends light as a lens does, and a well-aligned mass draws a background source into a full Einstein ring.
block:climate_casing: Casing for a climate engine. Earth's climate balances about 340 W/m² of incoming sunlight against heat radiated back to space.
entity:hawking_imp: A small creature forever evaporating. Like a black hole, the smaller it gets the hotter it glows and the faster it radiates itself away.
entity:pulsar_wisp: A spinning wisp that flashes on a perfect beat, like the lighthouse beam of a pulsar. Millisecond pulsars keep time nearly as well as atomic clocks.
block:aerosol_sprayer: Breaks liquid into droplets fine enough to hang in the air for days. The same kind of haze turns Titan orange and hides its surface from view.
block:bec_trap: A magnetic bottle for atoms cooled to billionths of a degree, where thousands of them fall into one quantum state and move as a single wave.
block:capacitor_bank: Rows of capacitors charged slowly and emptied all at once: energy gathered over seconds, released in microseconds as a single heavy pulse.
block:colloid_cell: A thin glass cell of fine grains in water. Unseen molecules jostle them endlessly; in 1908 Perrin watched that jitter and counted the atoms in a mole.
block:crystal_interferometer_mount: A rigid, damped cradle for an interferometer cut from one perfect silicon crystal. A neutron splits inside it, and a shake of an atom's width spoils the fringes.
block:dense_mass_core: A mass packed so tightly that time itself runs slow around it. Clocks set nearby lose seconds to the rest of the world, and never get them back.
block:doppler_drive: Moves a gamma source at speeds of a fraction of a micrometre per second, so its Doppler shift can cancel the tiny shift that gravity puts on its light.
block:evaporator_shield: Lead-lined housing for a radioactive evaporator. The water boils away cleanly; everything dangerous it carried stays behind, and stays concentrated.
block:geode_shell: A hollow stone lined with crystals that grew inward, one layer at a time, from mineral-rich water seeping through the cavity over ages.
block:helium3_detector: A tube of helium-3 gas. A slow neutron splits a nucleus into a proton and a triton with 764 keV between them, and the gas lights up with charge.
block:interferometer: Splits a beam of light, sends the halves down two paths and brings them back together. A change in path of a fraction of a wavelength moves the fringes.
block:lens_array_block: A grid of lenses working side by side, each forming its own small image of the scene. Together they see from many points at once.
block:markov_vat: A vat whose contents change from one state to the next by chance alone. Where they go next depends only on where they are now, never on how they got there.
block:mossbauer_absorber: Iron-57 bound so firmly in its crystal that it soaks up 14.4 keV gamma rays without recoil, a resonance sharp enough to feel one part in a thousand trillion.
block:pair_source: A laser through a nonlinear crystal. Now and then one photon splits into two whose polarisations are entangled: measure one and the other is already decided.
block:press_ram: The working piston of a hydraulic press. A small pump pushes on a broad face, and Pascal's principle multiplies the force by the ratio of their areas.
block:pull_shaft: A slow, steady drive that draws its load upward at a controlled rate. In a crystal puller it lifts the seed exactly as fast as the crystal grows.
block:rail_conductor: One of a pair of heavy rails. Current runs up one, across the armature and back down the other, and the magnetic force flings the armature along them.
block:salt_heat_exchanger: Passes heat between molten salt and water. Nitrate salt stays liquid from about 220 to 565 °C, so it can carry heat that would boil water off at once.
block:solar_receiver: The target at the focus of a mirror field, built to drink in concentrated sunlight. At Odeillo such a focus reaches some 3,500 °C.
block:telescope_tube: Holds a telescope's mirrors in exact alignment and is blackened inside, so the only light that reaches the focus is light from the sky.
block:test_mass_chamber: A vacuum chamber that hangs a polished fused-silica mirror on fine fibres, isolated from every tremor so it moves only when spacetime does.
block:unruh_detector: An accelerating detector should feel empty space as warm. It is a faint warmth: one kelvin takes an acceleration of some 10^20 metres per second squared.
block:xray_cabinet: A lead-lined, interlocked box that keeps X-rays in. Opening the door cuts the tube, so the only thing exposed is the sample.
item:pressure_suit_helmet: A sealed helmet that keeps the head in breathable pressure. Above about 19 km, water in the body would boil at body temperature without it.
item:refractory_suit_helmet: A helmet lined with ceramic that shrugs off heat which would melt steel. It insulates, so the inside stays cool while the outside glows.
item:whipple_shield_helmet: A thin outer bumper set apart from the shell, as Fred Whipple proposed in 1946. A fast grain strikes it, shatters into a spray, and spends itself in the gap.
block:asteroid_rock: The rubble of planetesimals that never became planets. Its chondrules are frozen droplets from the Solar System's first few million years.
fluid:mod_essence: Every fluid of one mod distilled together into a single liquid. It tastes, reportedly, of everything its authors ever put in a tank.
block:warp_casing: Hull plating for a warp field forge. An Alcubierre bubble would need negative energy density in its walls, which is what makes this casing exotic.
entity:fission_husk: A heavy, unstable shell of uranium-dark stone. It is always close to splitting, and when it goes it breaks into two lighter pieces and a burst of heat.
entity:plume_elemental: A column of hot rock rising from the base of the mantle, solid yet flowing over the ages. Where such a plume reaches the crust, chains of volcanoes follow.
block:hilbert_locker: Always full, and always room for one more. Move each item up one shelf, and the first shelf is free again, however many there are.
fluid:heavy_water: Water whose hydrogen is deuterium. It is about 11% denser than ordinary water, freezes at 3.8 °C, and slows neutrons without swallowing them.
block:reactor_vessel_casing: Thick steel for a reactor's pressure vessel. It must hold the core for decades while neutrons slowly make the metal more brittle.
block:corundum_crystal: Aluminium oxide crystallised in bulk, second only to diamond among common minerals for hardness. A trace of chromium makes it ruby; others, sapphire.
fluid:brownian_suspension: Fine clay held in water and never at rest: each grain is kicked about by molecules too small to see, and wanders without ever settling on a path.
block:weaver_casing: Casing for a machine that stitches with entanglement. Two particles that share one state stay linked, however far apart the weave carries them.
block:refinery_casing: Casing for a refinery that runs on chance. Each stage passes its product to the next by probability alone, and the averages come out exact.
block:chronal_accelerator: Time runs faster for everything in its field, and the universe sends the bill. Each borrowed tick must be paid for, in energy and in Chronon Gas.
fluid:quantum_spacetime_condensate: Spacetime treated as a fluid of quanta. In loop quantum gravity, area comes in discrete chunks, and here those chunks have settled into one shared state.
block:absolute_pedestal: A pedestal of the highest grade, made to hold an offering at the very centre of a ritual. Nothing set on it is ever quite where it was before.
block:bulk_cache: Bigger on the inside: it borrows a little room from a fifth dimension. In brane cosmology our whole universe floats in such a bulk.
entity:lens_phantom: Nearly invisible: it is seen only by how it bends the light behind it into arcs and rings, the way unseen dark matter betrays itself to telescopes.
entity:tidal_stretcher: A creature of the tide near a compact mass, where feet are pulled harder than head. It draws everything near it out long and thin, like spaghetti.
block:alt_az_mount: A mount that turns a dish on two simple axes, altitude and azimuth, while a computer works out how to follow the sky. Nearly every large modern telescope sits on one.
block:bending_magnet: A dipole magnet that curves a beam of charged particles along an arc. The faster the beam or the tighter the turn, the stronger the field it needs.
block:central_solenoid: The tall coil at a tokamak's core. Ramping its current induces the plasma current, so the plasma itself is the secondary winding of a giant transformer.
block:concentrator_mirror: A great curved array of mirrors that gathers light from a field of heliostats onto one focus. The Odeillo furnace reaches about 3,500 °C this way.
block:cyclotron_dee: One of a cyclotron's two hollow D-shaped electrodes. The RF voltage across the gap between them kicks each particle every half turn, so it spirals outward ever faster.
block:derrick_frame: The tall frame over a well that carries the crown block and the whole string of pipe. The word comes from Derrick, a seventeenth-century Tyburn hangman.
block:drill_string: Lengths of steel pipe screwed end to end that turn the bit and carry mud down to it. Kilometres of it wind up like a spring before the bit begins to turn.
block:exhaust_stack: A tall brick chimney. The hot gas inside is lighter than the air outside, so the taller the stack, the harder it draws.
block:goniometer: A precision turntable that sets sample and detector at exact angles. The detector swings twice as far as the crystal, keeping θ and 2θ in step.
block:horizon_cage: A cage of fields for something with no surface to grip. A black hole cannot be touched, so it must be held by its charge alone.
block:iridium_crucible: A crucible of iridium, which melts at 2,446 °C and shrugs off most molten oxides. Laser crystals such as YAG are pulled from melts held in one.
block:lens_grinder: A turning lap that wears glass into a curve with ever finer grit, then polishes it. Spinoza earned part of his living at one.
block:mhd_electrode: An electrode lining a magnetohydrodynamic channel. Conducting fluid swept through a magnetic field drives current straight into it, with no turbine at all.
block:neutron_guide: A tube whose walls reflect slow neutrons at grazing angles, much as a glass fibre carries light. Guides lead beams tens of metres from a reactor to the instruments.
block:peridotite: The dense green rock of the upper mantle, mostly olivine. Brought up into water and air, it slowly drinks them in and turns to serpentinite.
block:primary_mirror_cell: The cradle that holds a telescope's main mirror, propping its back at many points so the glass does not sag out of shape as the tube tilts.
block:radio_dish_panel: One curved panel of a radio dish. Its surface need only be true to a small fraction of the wavelength, so for long waves even wire mesh will do.
block:refractory_firebox: A fire chamber lined with firebrick, which keeps its strength far above the heat that slumps common brick. The fire stays in, and most of the heat does too.
block:satellite_wreck: The scorched frame and panels of a satellite that came down. Most burn up on re-entry; this one did not, quite.
block:step_laser: A laser whose pulse makes a moving step in the refractive index of glass. Light trying to overtake the step is slowed to a halt at it: an event horizon for light.
block:tesla_primary: A few turns of heavy copper fed by a capacitor and a spark gap. Tuned to the secondary, it rings its energy across into the tall coil beside it.
block:tilt_table: A table that tilts a neutron interferometer about its beam. In 1975 one let Colella, Overhauser and Werner see gravity shift a single neutron's quantum phase.
block:vacuum_beam_tube: Steel tube pumped to ultra-high vacuum, so a laser crosses kilometres with no stray gas to jitter its phase. LIGO's arms hold nearly 10,000 m³ of it.
block:xray_tube: Electrons slammed into a copper anode knock out inner electrons, and copper's sharp Kα X-ray line shines out as others fall in. Nearly all the rest ends as heat.
item:pressure_suit_leggings: Layered leggings that hold air pressure against the body. Bending a knee in an inflated suit is hard work, so the joints are built to keep their volume constant.
item:refractory_suit_leggings: Leggings of ceramic fibre under aluminised cloth, like a furnace worker's. The bright outer layer reflects radiant heat before it can soak in.
item:whipple_shield_leggings: Leggings layered like a Whipple shield: a thin outer skin shatters a hypervelocity grain into a spray of vapour that the next layer catches.
block:nebular_ice: Water, carbon monoxide and ammonia frozen together on dust grains at about fifteen kelvin. Starlight slowly builds larger molecules within it.
block:pulsar_crust: Iron from a neutron star's crust: a lattice of nuclei in a sea of electrons, held under a field of some hundred million tesla.
fluid:basaltic_magma: Molten rock low in silica, at around 1,200 °C. Runny for a magma, it pours out in fast rivers of lava rather than exploding, as on Hawaii.
block:garnet_crystal: A mass of garnet, the dodecahedral silicate that grows where rock is buried and heated. Its zoned layers record the pressures it passed through.
fluid:supercritical_water: Water above 374 °C and 22 MPa, where liquid and steam become one. It dissolves oils that ordinary water will not, and corrodes most metals.
block:transcendent_cache: A locker past every infinity the lesser caches count to. What it holds is not so much stored as asserted to exist.
block:leaded_glass: Glass with lead oxide melted in, often over half by weight. Lead's dense electron clouds stop X-rays and gamma rays while visible light passes through.
fluid:spent_fuel_salt: Molten fluoride fuel after a pass through the core, thick with fission products and fresh plutonium, and still hot with its own decay heat.
block:growth_furnace_casing: The insulated shell of a crystal-growth furnace. Its job is calm: the steadier the heat around the melt, the fewer flaws freeze into the crystal.
block:pulsed_lab_casing: Steel walls lined with mesh, built to keep the sharp spikes of pulsed experiments in and stray radio noise out. A Faraday cage, in effect.
block:burst_casing: The shell of an observatory that waits for bursts lasting milliseconds that never repeat. It is built to sit very still for a very long time.
block:resonance_pedestal: A pedestal tuned to ring in sympathy with its neighbours, as a wine glass sings to a matching note. The first and plainest of its kind.
fluid:dark_era_haze: What is left in the Dark Era, after the last black hole has evaporated: a thin gas of photons, neutrinos and stray leptons, cooling forever.
fluid:strained_spacetime: Spacetime under tidal strain: stretched along one line and squeezed across it, as the Moon stretches the oceans. Anything inside it is pulled apart.
fluid:reheating_plasma: The hot soup left when the inflaton decayed and inflation ended. It filled a cold, empty universe with particles and heat: the Big Bang proper.
block:chamber_casing: The shell of a chamber where time runs at another rate. Even on Earth, a clock a kilometre higher gains about one part in 10¹³.
block:armature_breech: The loading end of a railgun, where the conducting armature sits across the rails. A megaamp pulse closes the circuit and the Lorentz force flings it down the bore.
block:bitter_plate_stack: Perforated copper discs stacked in a helix, as Francis Bitter designed in the 1930s. Water rushes through the holes to carry off the heat of tens of kiloamps.
block:centrifuge_rotor: A thin-walled cylinder spun so fast its rim outruns sound. Heavier molecules crowd towards the wall and lighter ones drift to the axis.
block:control_rod_drive: The mechanism that raises and lowers a reactor's boron rods. If power fails it simply lets go, and gravity drops the rods into the core.
block:cyclotron_yoke: The iron return path of a cyclotron magnet. It carries the flux back from pole to pole, so the field across the gap stays strong and even.
block:dish_truss: The steel frame behind a radio dish. It must hold the surface true to a fraction of a wavelength while the whole dish tilts and sags under its own weight.
block:entanglement_node: A junction that keeps entangled pairs until they are wanted. Their correlations are perfect, yet no message can ride on them: no-signalling sees to that.
block:feed_horn: A flared metal waveguide at the focus of a dish. It funnels the faint reflected radio waves into the receiver and turns a deaf ear to whatever comes from the sides.
block:graphite_moderator_block: Pure graphite slows fission neutrons by collision with carbon nuclei, which seldom absorb them. Chicago Pile-1 was a stack of such blocks, in 1942.
block:horizon_containment: Walls built to hold a region where escape velocity reaches light speed. Nothing leaves through a horizon; the walls are for what has not fallen in yet.
block:jet_collimator: A magnetic nozzle that pinches a plasma flow into a narrow beam, much as twisted field lines are thought to shape the jets of quasars and young stars.
block:lens_pylon: A mast that holds mass where its curvature bends passing light. A gravitational lens has no single focal point: it brings light together along a line.
block:mhd_field_magnet: The magnet across an MHD channel. Conducting fluid driven through its field makes current at right angles to both, and the output rises with the square of the field.
block:observatory_dome: A rotating hemispherical roof with a shuttered slit, turned to keep pace with the telescope so it always looks out through the opening.
block:polished_cherenkov_quartz: Quartz polished to carry Cherenkov light, the blue glow given off when a charged particle outruns light in the glass, at about two-thirds of c.
block:proof_floor: Flat, even and featureless, like the axioms beneath a theorem. Everything above it stands only because it does not give way.
block:radiometer_mast: A mast of radiometers weighing incoming sunlight against outgoing heat. A planet's climate hangs on that balance, a few watts per square metre either way.
block:return_rift: A tear in space that leads back the way it came. Of all the doors in these places, it is the one that always opens onto home.
block:scintillator_panel: A sheet that gives a brief flash of light whenever a charged particle passes through. Walls of them catch cosmic-ray showers as they rain down.
block:stochastic_core: A bank of random sources for Monte Carlo sums. The error falls as one over the square root of the samples: a hundred times the dice for ten times the accuracy.
block:tesla_secondary: The tall, finely wound coil of a Tesla transformer. Tuned to resonate with the primary, it builds hundreds of kilovolts at its crown.
block:toroidal_field_coil: One of the D-shaped coils that ring a tokamak. Together they make the strong field running the long way round the torus, holding the plasma off the walls.
block:vacuum_vessel: The sealed doughnut-shaped chamber of a tokamak, pumped below a billionth of an atmosphere before fuel is let in, so the plasma meets nothing but itself.
item:pressure_suit_boots: Sealed boots of a pressure suit. Above about 19 km, the Armstrong limit, water boils at body temperature, and so would the wearer without them.
item:refractory_suit_boots: Boots lined with refractory ceramic, the kind that keeps its strength at temperatures that melt steel and lets very little of the heat through.
item:whipple_shield_boots: Armoured like a spacecraft: a thin outer bumper shatters an incoming particle into a spray the inner wall can stop. Fred Whipple proposed it in 1946.
block:antistone_bricks: Antistone dressed into bricks. Among antimatter it is as sound as any masonry; a single ordinary atom touching it would annihilate with it.
block:rim_slag: Cinder flung from the inner edge of an accretion disk, where gas spirals in at a fair fraction of light speed and is heated to millions of degrees.
block:hyperreal_cache: Its walls obey whatever law is currently in force. The contents, like infinitesimals beside the real numbers, sit at a scale no ordinary rule can reach.
block:crustal_rock: Silicate rock of a planet's crust, the thin cool skin over the mantle: on Earth about 7 km thick beneath the oceans and 35 km under the continents.
entity:geodynamo_wraith: A drifting presence of churning iron and current, the geodynamo given shape. Like Earth's own field, it wanders, and now and then flips its poles.
fluid:maxwell_boltzmann_gas: An ideal gas whose molecular speeds follow the Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution: most move near the typical speed, with a long thin tail of very fast ones.
block:cascade_casing: Shielded housing for a centrifuge cascade. Each stage enriches uranium only slightly, so stages are piped in series by the dozen and machines run by the thousand.
fluid:molten_salt_fuel: Uranium and plutonium dissolved in molten fluoride salt, fuel and coolant at once, flowing at low pressure. Oak Ridge ran a reactor on it from 1965 to 1969.
fluid:tritium: Hydrogen with two neutrons, radioactive with a half-life of 12.3 years. Its beta electrons are so weak they cannot get through the outer layer of skin.
block:moissanite_crystal: Silicon carbide, found by Henri Moissan in a meteorite crater in 1893. Nearly as hard as diamond, it splits light into colours even more strongly.
block:foam_cache: Held together by a bubble of stable vacuum. Spacetime at the Planck scale may seethe with fluctuations; inside, it has been made to keep still.
block:convergence_altar: A focus for the pedestals around it, which give up what they hold to a single point, as rays meet at the focus of a lens.
block:tokamak_casing: Lead-lined shell for a fusion hall. Deuterium-tritium fusion sends out 14.1 MeV neutrons that pass through anything thin, so these walls are not.
block:ejecta_cache: Thrown out of a white hole with everything else. A white hole is a black hole run backwards: nothing can enter, so this has never been opened from outside.
fluid:tidal_plasma: Plasma near a black hole, where the pull on its near side far outstrips the far. Infalling gas is drawn out into long, thin streams: spaghettified.
entity:binary_serpent: Two bodies coiled round each other in a tightening spiral, shedding gravitational waves. Each turn is faster than the last, until the chirp ends in a merger.
block:chance_tiles: Tiles laid in no repeating order, each pattern drawn at random. Any stretch that looks designed is a coincidence the dice were always going to throw.
fluid:autocatalytic_broth: A soup of molecules that catalyse their own making: each copy speeds the making of the next, so the broth grows faster the more of it there is.
fluid:renormalised_essence: Essence with its infinities taken away, the way renormalisation tames the endless sums of quantum field theory until only finite, measurable values remain.
fluid:antihydrogen: A positron bound to an antiproton. CERN first made a few atoms of it in 1995; it can only be held in magnetic traps, since touching any wall annihilates it.
block:antistone: Stone made of antimatter, the mirror image of ordinary rock. It looks exactly the same; only meeting matter would tell the difference, and then not for long.
fluid:antiwater: Water with every proton, neutron and electron swapped for its antiparticle. It would boil, freeze and flow just like water, as long as nothing ordinary touched it.
fluid:liquid_antihelium: Antihelium cooled to a liquid. Only a handful of antihelium nuclei have ever been detected in collider debris; a whole pool of it should not exist.
block:accretion_casing: Casing built to sit beside an accretion disk, where infalling gas heats to millions of degrees and shines in X-rays before it crosses the horizon.
fluid:accretion_disk_plasma: Gas spiralling into a black hole, heated by friction to millions of kelvin. On the way down it can turn tens of percent of its rest mass into light.
fluid:interstellar_medium: The thin gas between the stars, about one atom per cubic centimetre: a better vacuum than any made on Earth, yet the stuff new stars are born from.
fluid:molecular_cloud: Cold, dense gas where hydrogen pairs into molecules and dust shields them from starlight. At ten kelvin it collapses, slowly, into new stars.
block:station_hull: Aluminium skin and stringers from a spacecraft, thin enough to dent by hand. In vacuum, a few millimetres of it is all that separates air from nothing.
fluid:liquid_sodium: Sodium melted at 98 °C. It carries heat far better than water and boils only at 883 °C, which is why fast reactors use it as coolant, though it burns in air.
fluid:ferrofluid: Magnetic nanoparticles suspended in oil. Near a magnet it rises into spikes along the field lines; NASA developed it in the 1960s to steer rocket fuel in weightlessness.
fluid:magnetized_plasma: Plasma threaded by magnetic field lines. Its charged particles spiral along them and cannot cross, so a field can hold a gas hotter than the Sun's core.
block:mhd_channel_casing: The duct of a magnetohydrodynamic generator. Hot conducting gas rushes through a magnetic field, and current is drawn straight off electrodes in its walls, with no turbine at all.
block:absolute_frame_casing: A frame that keeps its shape whatever the laws around it do: the one fixed reference in a place where every other measure has come loose.
block:logos_coil_block: A coil wound of Logos Thread, the word that puts things in order. Current through it does not so much make a field as insist on one.
